key_insight: A thin (~150 µm) single-crystal organometal halide perovskite detector can directly detect high-energy charged particles in the hundreds of MeV range.
engineering_relevance: This suggests perovskites could enable simpler, low-cost radiation tracking and real-time monitoring devices integrated directly on patterned or curved electronics.
method: Grew a thin single perovskite crystal on a patterned substrate using a dewetting technique.
Coupled the detector to dedicated electronics matched to the crystal’s timing response.
Tested performance under high-energy charged-particle flux across a wide dynamic range.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports the first demonstration of a thin OMHP single crystal detecting high-energy charged particles of hundreds of MeV over a high dynamic range of incident fluxes.
watch_item: The result is a first demonstration, so scalability, long-term radiation durability, and reproducibility still need validation.
paper_title: Thin single-crystal perovskite detector for high-energy charged particles
